item.description: arXiv:2601.20553v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a fully quantum field-theoretic framework for gravitational wave (GW) detection, describing the interaction as inelastic photon-graviton scattering. We demonstrate that for \textit{a coherent graviton state}, this microscopic model explicitly reproduces the standard classical geometric-optics time delay, providing a rigorous consistency test of the correspondence limit. We propose a detection scheme based on Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, where the GW-induced spectral shifts render entangled photon pairs distinguishable. This encodes the gravitational signal into the modulation of photon coincidence rates --- a quantum observable robust against laser intensity noise. Furthermore, we show that non-classical graviton states, such as squeezed states, induce unique decoherence signatures, establishing theoretical bounds on gravitational decoherence and defining the operational limits for probing the quantum nature of gravity.
item.dc:creator: K. Hari (IIT Bombay), S. Shankaranarayanan (IIT Bombay)

item.title: Bootstrapping Fermionic $R$-operators with Decorated Yang--Baxter Equations
item.description: arXiv:2603.11172v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Integrating infinitesimal generators of local dynamics into finite-time evolution is generally harder than extracting a local Hamiltonian from a quantum gate. For integrable one-dimensional quantum many-body systems, a recent bootstrap constructs one-parameter $R$-operators directly from Hamiltonians satisfying the Reshetikhin condition. However, this condition excludes important models such as the Hubbard model, whose two-parameter $R$-operator was obtained by Shastry from a decorated Yang--Baxter equation obeyed by its free-fermion sector. Here, I extend the bootstrap to $R$-operators constrained by both the ordinary and decorated Yang--Baxter equations. Their joint expansion produces additional Hamiltonian-level necessary conditions and recursively determines candidate higher-order terms, subject to two-site locality at each order. I also derive compatibility and factorization conditions under which a Shastry-type superposition solves the $RLL$ relation after deformation by an onsite involution. The construction recovers the known two-parameter $R$-operators of the Hubbard and XYh models, whose full Yang--Baxter equations follow from established tetrahedral Zamolodchikov algebra relations. For a superconducting Hubbard deformation, the scalar equations are generically incompatible, placing it outside this framework. These results provide diagnostics and a systematic route to fermionic $R$-operators beyond the Reshetikhin condition. General sufficiency, convergence of the formal bootstrap, and sufficiency of the deformation conditions remain open.
item.dc:creator: Zhao Zhang

item.title: Optimization of entanglement harvesting with arbitrary temporal profiles: the limit of second order perturbation theory
item.description: arXiv:2604.06303v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the protocol of entanglement harvesting when two local probes couple to the vacuum of a real scalar quantum field with arbitrary temporal profiles. We use a Hermite expansion to efficiently compute smeared field propagators in closed-form, recasting the negativity between the probes as a matrix product. We then optimize the protocol under different signalling conditions, enhancing entanglement harvesting by several orders of magnitude. This optimization would take current experimental proposals beyond the regime of second order perturbation theory.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Morote-Balboa, T. Rick Perche

item.title: Collective Kernel EFT for Pre-activation ResNets
item.description: arXiv:2604.15742v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In finite-width deep neural networks, the empirical kernel $G$ evolves stochastically across layers. We develop a collective kernel effective field theory (EFT) for a simplified pre-activation residual model. Exact conditional Gaussianity of the residual increment gives finite-width discrete identities for $G$ and its sigma-kernel source. A projected $G$-only closure and a continuous-depth approximation define reference equations for the mean kernel $K_0$, the kernel covariance $V_4$, and the next-to-leading mean correction $K_1$. Numerical tests show that this closure captures the leading mean-kernel evolution, whereas its covariance and next-to-leading accuracy depend on sigma-kernel modes omitted from the $G$-only state. For the scalar ($N=1$) model with $\tanh$ activation, a Hermite--Galerkin extension agrees with the extrapolated $K_1$ value and reduces the $V_4$ endpoint error by $85$--$93\%$ relative to the $G$-only reference. These results clarify the range of validity of the equal-time Markov $G$-only description and identify the additional collective information required beyond it.
item.dc:creator: Hidetoshi Kawase, Toshihiro Ota

item.title: Tunneling from an oscillating state in quantum mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2605.04139v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the decay of general initial states out of a metastable potential well in quantum mechanics. We provide a closed-form expression for the probability current that tunnels through the barrier in terms of the resonant states into which the initial state can be decomposed. All ingredients are computed analytically to first subleading order in the semiclassical limit. Specializing to a coherently-oscillating state, we derive an equivalent semiclassical approximation to the current via the path integral, which circumvents the decomposition into resonant states. We test the accuracy of the approximation by comparing it to a numerical solution of the Schr\"odinger equation.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Janssen, Matthew Kleban, Cameron Norton

item.title: Machine Learning Approaches to Building Quantum Circuits for Sets of Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2605.06633v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Machine learning nowadays becomes a useful instrument in many subjects. In this paper we use interpretable machine learning to build quantum algorithm. By studying the parameters of the machine learning algorithm we were able to construct universal shortest analytic quantum algorithm for arbitrary diagonal matrix of any size.
item.dc:creator: Matvei Fedin, Andrey Morozov

item.title: Pole Skipping, Avoided Crossing, and Resonant Excitation in Kerr Quasinormal Modes near Algebraically Special Frequencies
item.description: arXiv:2605.17840v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Kerr quasinormal modes near algebraically special frequencies exhibit anomalous behavior, including apparent bifurcation, disappearance, and a nonsmooth connection to the Schwarzschild limit, which has remained puzzling for decades. Tracking poles and zeros of Green-function building blocks across different Riemann sheets, we show that the bifurcation is due to an avoided crossing accompanied by resonant excitation, while the disappearance is due to pole skipping caused by cancellation of a quasinormal-mode pole by a Matsubara-mode zero. This resolves the physical origin of these long-standing anomalies.
item.dc:creator: Kei-ichiro Kubota, Hayato Motohashi

item.title: Shadow, Emission, and Strong-Field Lensing of Dilatonic Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2606.17284v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the shadow and strong-field optical properties of a static, spherically symmetric dyon-like dilatonic black hole. The photon sphere radius, critical impact parameter, and shadow radius are obtained and analyzed in terms of the charge $Q$ and the dilatonic coupling parameter $a$. We show that increasing these parameters decreases the photon sphere and shadow radii, leading to a smaller apparent shadow. The predicted angular diameter is compared with the observational data for M87$^{*}$ and SgrA$^{*}$. We explicitly show that the Sgr A* data do not constrain the model parameters, whereas the results for M87* depend on the adopted mass estimates from stellar and gas dynamics. We also estimate the high-frequency energy emission rate in the geometric-optics approximation and derive the leading Bozza coefficient $\bar{a}$, which characterizes the logarithmic behavior of the deflection angle in the strong-field regime. Astrophysical implication of the obtained outcomes are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Kuantay Boshkayev, Ainur Urazalina, Aidana Kurmanbek, Manas Khassanov, Daniya Utepova

item.title: Mass-Varying Dark Matter Induced Scalarization and Scalar Clouds around Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2606.29864v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a black hole solution embedded in a mass-varying dark matter (DM) halo and study scalarization induced by DM. We derive the required conditions on the scalar DM coupling that allow for a regular bound-state scalar cloud. We find that such configurations exist only for quantized coupling values in terms of the halo's intrinsic parameters (for Hernquist, this reduces to the inverse of the compactness). This study provides a novel connection between DM phenomenology and scalarization around a black hole.
item.dc:creator: H. Mohseni Sadjadi, M. Navid Gasemi Zad

item.title: Harmonic oscillation and orbital morphology for spinning charged quantum corrected black hole
item.description: arXiv:2607.17658v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This study investigates the dynamical behavior of particle's test around a spinning charged Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton (EMd) quantum corrected black hole (QCBH) by examining the effects of spinning parameter $a$, quantum correction parameter $b$, and charge parameter $Q$. Using EMd spacetime geometry, we analyze the effective potential and effective force to determine the stability and structure of the circular orbits in a strong gravitational field. Furthermore, we calculate the oscillation frequencies radial $(\Omega_r)$, vertical $(\Omega_\theta)$, and angular $(\Omega_\phi)$, as well as the corresponding Periapsis and Lense-Thirring precession frequencies. The spin parameter primarily determines the spinning properties of spacetime, while the quantum correction and charge particle introduce additional biases to Kerr-Newman geometry, particularly near the event horizon. These corrections alter the position and stability of the circular orbits, and the spectrum effectively associates with particle's motion. The results provide a comprehensive description of the orbital dynamics of spinning EMd QCBH through future high-precision astrophysical observations.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: R. Khalid, M. Yasir, S. Qaisar, and F. Javed, Eur. Phys. J. C (2026) 86:1243
item.dc:creator: Rameez Khalid, Muhammad Yasir, Shahid Qaisar, Faisal Javed

item.title: Free energy and spectral edge of the SYK model
item.description: arXiv:2607.18998v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Consider the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model with $N$ Majorana fermions and interaction order $q$. For even $4\leq q\ll \sqrt{N}$, we present a microscopic framework that determines the free energy limit at every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>0$. In particular, this gives the first rigorous derivation of the Schwinger-Dyson thermodynamics of the model. For all even $q\in \{4,6,...,N-4\}$, we further determine the asymptotic location of the largest eigenvalue, which answers a question posed by Feng-Tian-Wei \cite{FengTianWei1}. Consequently, we obtained the free energy limit along every sequence $\beta\equiv \beta_N\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Yukun He

item.title: Affine Extension of the Free-Particle--Oscillator--Inverted-Oscillator Triangle
item.description: arXiv:2607.20711v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the one-dimensional linear-potential system as an affine extension of the conformal triangle formed by the free particle, harmonic oscillator (HO) and inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Unlike these homogeneous quadratic Hamiltonians in the $sl(2,\mathbb R)$ sector, the linear-potential Hamiltonian involves the Heisenberg ideal of the Schr\"odinger algebra. Its direct relation to the free particle is a regular accelerated-frame transformation, developed here at the levels of the classical action, canonical transformation, wave-function intertwiner and propagator; its HO and IHO realizations instead arise through singular displaced-oscillator limits. The Airy energy eigenstates follow from a cubic-phase transform of free-particle momentum eigenstates, from condensation of highly excited harmonic-oscillator levels, and from the limit of a subdominant parabolic-cylinder scattering branch of the inverted oscillator. We also develop a planar extension in homogeneous crossed electric and magnetic fields, where uniform acceleration generates the electric interaction, while uniform rotation produces the Landau coupling and the centrifugal inverted-oscillator term; the guiding-center dynamics yields the Hall drift.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Alcala, Mikhail S. Plyushchay

item.title: Static multipolar Einstein-vector-Gauss-Bonnet black holes
item.description: arXiv:2608.11900v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct and analyze static multipolar black holes in Einstein-vector-Gauss-Bonnet theory with a quadratic coupling function. The vectorized solutions bifurcate from the Schwarzschild black hole at discrete values of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, obtained from a perturbative eigenvalue problem on the Schwarzschild background and labelled by the angular multipole number $\ell$. We restrict to the fundamental radial branches. The electric sector contains the known spherically symmetric $\ell=0$ branch as well as axisymmetric branches with $\ell>0$. These electric branches extend to larger values of the coupling. The magnetic sector features a sequence of axisymmetric branches, including the previously found magnetic dipole branch at $\ell=0$. The magnetic branches instead exist only on finite intervals of the coupling, ending at critical solutions. Away from the bifurcation point, nonlinearities generate additional multipoles, but even-$\ell$ and odd-$\ell$ moments remain separated.
item.dc:creator: Burkhard Kleihaus, Jutta Kunz

item.title: Theoretical Aspects of Direct Waves in Kerr Black Holes: Pole-Splitting Method for Ringdown Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2609.11908v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a theoretical description of direct waves (DWs) from a particle plunging into a Kerr black hole in the extreme-mass-ratio regime. A DW is characterized by a source-driven complex frequency $\omega_{\rm G}$ that reflects the particle's orbital motion, including motion inside the ergoregion. Hence, it is expected to be a probe of rich structures of Kerr black holes. We show that the contribution of the quasinormal-mode (QNM) pole sector to the DW is part of dynamical QNM excitation. We also show that the apparent horizon-mode poles cancel at every order of a consistent near-horizon expansion of the trajectory, homogeneous radial solution, and complete point-particle source. This result assumes that the point particle follows a geodesic near the horizon and leaves open the possibility of a transient DW while the particle passes near the ergosurface or the vicinity of the potential barrier. To investigate this possibility in simulated plunge waveforms, we develop a pole-splitting method that decomposes the transfer function into QNM-pole and non-pole parts. The resulting waveform decomposition avoids the frequency-dependent time shift (group delay) introduced by the QNM filtering. For quasi-circular plunges into moderately and rapidly rotating Kerr black holes, the frequency and decay rate of the non-pole waveform show qualitative agreement with our theoretical prediction over finite time intervals. These results support the potential use of DWs as probes of the ergoregion and gravitational redshift effect around black holes.
item.dc:creator: Nao Nakamoto, Naritaka Oshita, Hiroki Takeda

item.title: Non-stabilizerness and entanglement in $(2+1)$-dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory using tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2609.28634v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study non-stabilizerness (magic) in the ground state of $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Hamiltonian lattice gauge theory with matter, formulated in the dressed-site basis in the hardcore-gluon truncation and restricted to the zero baryon-number sector. Using matrix product states, we compute three facets of magic: the second-order stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE) $M_2$, its non-local component $M_2^{\rm NL}$, estimated by the SRE $M_2(\tilde\psi)$ of the computational-basis Schmidt representative $\tilde\psi$, and a lower bound in terms of the anti-flatness $F$ of the entanglement spectrum. We also prove a stronger form of the sandwich relation: $-\log_2(1-4F)\le M_2^{\rm NL}\le M_2$; the lower bound rests on a stronger inequality that we obtain for arbitrary Schmidt bases and rank, with an optimal constant. Combined with recent results, this yields the unconditional bracket $\max\{-\log_2(1-4F),\,M_2(\tilde\psi)-4\}\le M_2^{\rm NL}\le M_2(\tilde\psi)$. We emphasize a structural distinction that makes the non-local quantities the physically preferred diagnostics: whereas the full SRE depends on the (non-unique) encoding of the gauge-invariant local Hilbert space into qubits, the non-local magic, its estimate $M_2(\tilde\psi)$, and the anti-flatness are invariant under site-local re-encodings and are therefore intrinsic to the state and bipartition. By varying the gauge coupling for two values of the fermion mass on lattices up to $8\times 8$ ($\sim 288$ qubits) with bond dimension up to $128$, we find that the non-local magic, as estimated by $M_2(\tilde\psi)$, furnishes a sharper and more bond-dimension-friendly probe of the gauge-matter delocalization crossover compared to the full SRE or the gauge-invariant entanglement entropy, retaining a clear signal at bond dimensions well below those needed to converge the ground state itself.

item.title: Two-horizon sector thermodynamics and NUT bi-hair in Kerr-Newman-NUT spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2609.33032v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: First law consistency alone does not determine the black hole state space of NUT-charged spacetimes, because several inequivalent macroscopic formulations can yield consistent thermodynamics. We develop a two-horizon sector diagnostic for the electrically charged Kerr-Newman-NUT family by organizing the inner- and outer-horizon entropies and inverse temperatures into sum ($\Sigma$) and difference ($\Delta$) sectors. The charged rotating geometry gives a more stringent test of the uncharged Taub-NUT sector result, since the mass $M$, ordinary electric charge $Q$, ordinary angular momentum $J$, NUT charge $N$, and the NUT secondary hair $J_N=MN$ all enter the same two-horizon thermodynamics. For the physically anchored minimal homogeneous state spaces defined and tested here, we find a clear sector separation: the $\Sigma$ sector closes with the charge-like variables $Q$ and $N$, whereas the $\Delta$ sector additionally requires the rotation-like variables $J$ and $J_N$. Natural reductions that eliminate either $J_N$ or $N$ fail to reproduce the first law coefficient fixed by the sector temperature, and their associated Bekenstein-Smarr relations do not close with the assigned scaling weights. Within this class, electric charge and ordinary rotation therefore do not absorb the NUT secondary response, and the charged rotating family supports the NUT bi-hair organization: $N$ has a charge-like sector role, while $J_N=MN$ is a rotation-like thermodynamic secondary hair. The latter is defined off shell in the homogeneous equation of state, not as a new metric parameter or asymptotic conserved charge.

item.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.19440v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.

item.title: Group averaging and the geometry of physical quantum states: from normalizable solutions to solvable loop quantum cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2610.24027v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In canonical quantum gravity the physical states solve the constraints but are typically not normalizable in the kinematical Hilbert space. Group averaging constructs them from normalizable kinematical seeds. We describe the geometry of this seed-to-state map in the language of geometric quantum mechanics. When averaging is an orthogonal projection, the admissible kinematical rays form a holomorphic vector bundle over the physical ray space. The embedded exact solutions form its zero section, and its fibers are strictly larger than gauge orbits. Observables descend to the base exactly when the Hessian of the squared constraint vanishes along their flow. For distributional physical states, group averaging on an explicit Sobolev test space yields an affine bundle of representatives. Its sections are embeddings of the physical ray space whose images contain no exact solutions. The test-space inner product singles out one of them, and narrowing the seed profile gives Weyl sequences of approximate solutions. We apply this to solvable loop quantum cosmology. Group averaging reproduces the Klein--Gordon physical inner product on an explicit test space. Because the scalar-field momentum enters the constraint quadratically, the constraint spectrum has an edge near the shell. The canonical section is then mode-dependent and not K\"ahler isometric, and the canonical seeds of small universes are biased off the shell. The edge also separates the Page--Wootters state from the slice of the Klein--Gordon solution. An ideal clock shows none of these effects. The results separate the canonical structures, namely physical rays, physical geometry and Dirac observables, from those that depend on a choice of seeds, test space or clock.

item.title: Ricci-flat Seeds, Trombone Rescaling and Magnetizing Kerr Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.30256v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a new family of Ricci-flat rotating metrics, which we refer to as Solution II, obtained by demagnetizing the genuine Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (G-KBR) black hole. Together with Solution I, which was previously obtained by demagnetizing the Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (KBR) black hole, this gives two families of Ricci-flat deformations of the Kerr black hole, each labeled by $B$. We study the global structures, thermodynamics, various limits, and the local connections among these limits. We also study the remagnetizations in both Einstein-Maxwell and Kaluza-Klein theories, and find that, to yield a physically acceptable solution, the Ernst transformation should be augmented by an appropriate trombone rescaling.

item.title: Thermomagnetic enhancement of conserved-charge correlations in a lattice-constrained PNJL model
item.description: arXiv:2610.30393v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Conserved-charge correlations offer a promising probe of magnetic fields in strongly interacting matter. We investigate their magnetic response and the finite-density equation of state within a lattice-constrained three-flavor Polyakov--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model. A thermomagnetic scalar coupling, inferred by Gaussian process regression from lattice QCD results for the average light-quark condensate, incorporates inverse magnetic catalysis into the effective interaction. Without fitting conserved-charge observables, the resulting framework substantially improves their magnetic-field dependence and crossover behavior compared with the fixed-coupling model. In particular, it captures the pronounced magnetic enhancement of the baryon--electric-charge correlation and related susceptibility ratios, supporting their use as QCD magnetometers. The comparison demonstrates that the medium dependence of the effective interaction is essential to describe this response within the model. We further calculate pressure Taylor coefficients through sixth order and reconstruct the pressure and baryon density at nonzero baryon chemical potential. Our results show that lattice information from a single chiral observable constrains a broad thermodynamic response, connecting inverse magnetic catalysis, conserved-charge correlations, and the equation of state in a common framework. This provides a lattice-constrained basis for investigating magnetic-field signatures and finite-density thermodynamics in QCD matter.
